prompts.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Asset: wide 16:9 watercolour background for an Ogmore Castle historical timeline. The supplied image is a style and landscape-composition reference, not a building to preserve. Match its loose transparent watercolour washes, cold-pressed ivory paper grain, soft blue-grey river, muted olive foliage and ochre stone palette. Create an explicitly interpretive impression of Ogmore's early-12th-century earth-and-timber phase beside the River Ewenny: a modest oval earthen ringwork with a low timber palisade and simple timber hall, beside a calm broad river in the foreground, wooded low hills behind. No stone keep or stone curtain wall yet. Keep an open, uncluttered stretch of water and grassy riverbank in the lower left for a later HTML overlay. No modern fence, paths, poles, vehicles or clothing. Do not show the formal stepping-stone alignment because its exact construction date is unknown. No battle, no people necessary, no fantasy towers, no text, no labels, no logos. The result should look like a companion painting to the supplied image, with subtle paper edges and natural painterly detail.

Use case: historical-scene. Asset: wide 16:9 watercolour background for an Ogmore Castle timeline. Use the supplied present-day painting as the style, landscape, river and rectangular keep location reference. Make a restrained artist's impression of Ogmore in the early 13th century after the addition of stone curtain walls. Reimagine the surviving rectangular Norman keep as a complete small limestone tower, roughly two to three storeys, surrounded by a modest low stone enclosure and simple timber-roofed domestic buildings; keep the character of a small Welsh Marcher stronghold, not a grand royal castle. A ditch surrounds the inner enclosure. Retain the broad river foreground, wooded background, pale blue sky, irregular olive and ochre washes, and tactile ivory paper of the reference. The precise roofs and missing portions are interpretive. Remove modern wire fences, posts, paths and poles. Leave the lower left visually quiet for an HTML caption. Avoid invented large round towers, Gothic spires, tall curtain walls or drawbridges across the river. Do not show a precisely dated formal stepping-stone row. No battle, no text, no lettering, no watermark.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: wide 16:9 watercolour companion view for a timeline about Ogmore and nearby Ewenni/Ewenny Priory. The supplied painting is a style reference only; paint a different nearby place. Depict a quiet exterior study of the surviving Ewenny Priory church: a low robust Norman Romanesque limestone church, cruciform body, sturdy square crossing tower, plain rounded arched openings and thick walls, seen across a grassy churchyard with restrained mature trees. Treat this as a present-day-inspired architectural study, not a claim to reproduce the exact 1141 appearance. No huge Gothic cathedral or needle spire, no elaborate fantasy monastery, no invented monks. Match the reference's soft moss greens, warm-grey stone, pale blue-grey sky, transparent granulated watercolour and textured ivory cold-pressed paper. The building should sit in the middle/right with quiet grass at lower left for an HTML overlay. No river or stepping stones needed in this view. No text, labels, signage, modern cars or watermark.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: wide 16:9 watercolour landscape for the surrounding-area chapters of an Ogmore history timeline. Supplied image is the style reference. Paint a present-day-inspired study of Merthyr Mawr Warren and the tidal lower valley: rolling pale sandy dunes partly covered with marram grass, soft green woodland on one edge, a gentle saltmarsh/river channel curving through the foreground, and a distant pale Bristol Channel horizon under a spacious sky. This is a landscape study, not a geographically exact map or a dated reconstruction. No castle, church, standing stones, prehistoric houses, modern buildings or invented archaeological structures. Match the same loose translucent olive, sage, warm sand and blue-grey water washes, broken natural pigment edges, ivory paper grain and gentle hand-painted detail as the reference. Keep the lower left quiet for HTML copy. No people needed, no text, labels or watermark.
